diagnosis: I calibrated the model with DDS on daily NSE over 1971–1997, after a one-year warm-up. The best set reached NSE 0.648, KGE 0.78 and r 0.81, with a volume bias of about −5%. I ran the same parameter set alone over 1987–1997, a window that falls inside the calibration period, so it is not an independent check; it gave NSE 0.655. Two independent DDS searches converged to about the same NSE (0.646 and 0.648) with quite different response and soil parameters (for example K0 0.99 vs 0.14 and LP 0.56 vs 0.97). This equifinality means the individual parameters are uncertain, although the simulated hydrographs perform alike. The fit levels off at an NSE around 0.65, which points to errors in the inputs or model structure rather than to the optimiser. Likely causes are snowmelt and rain-on-snow in the high Cairngorm headwaters (lumped temperature with a single TT), how much rain lands on the upland areas, and timing errors in flood peaks. The snow parameters (TT about 1.0 °C, CFMAX about 5, SFCF about 0.7, which reduces snowfall) take up some of this input bias. The volume bias in 1987–1997 was larger (about −10%). Expect a moderate NSE of about 0.6–0.65 in 1998–2008; winter and spring snowmelt peaks are the least reliable part of the simulation.
